title: Deleting a subprotocol returns nothing only for the whole protocol
statement: Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) producing values in $\alpha$, and suppose $s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$, as recorded by a subprotocol path from the root of $p$ down to the root of $s$. If splicing that path out of $p$ produces no protocol at all, then $s$ is in fact all of $p$; that is, $s = p$.
hypotheses_covered: a subprotocol path witnessing that s is a rooted subtree of p
deleting that path yields no protocol (the none result)
replaced:
If $\texttt{deletePath}\;\texttt{hsp} = \texttt{none}$, then $s = p$.  That is, deletion
returns \texttt{none} only when $s$ is the entire protocol $p$.
